views.name: classroom_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT classroom.building AS building,
       classroom.room_number AS room_number,
       classroom.capacity AS capacity
FROM classroom
views.description: One row per classroom with its building, room number, and capacity.
validated_on: Could you please gather a list of all the buildings, except 'Gates', along with the number of classrooms they contain? I really need to know the count of classrooms for each building!
For buildings linked to the Civil Engineering department, what are their names and average classroom capacities, ordered from highest to lowest average capacity?

Determine the number of classrooms categorized as 'Large', 'Medium', or 'Small' based on their capacities in the 'Lamberton' building, with only those classrooms having a capacity greater than 20 included in the count.

views.name: classroom_capacity_projection
views.body_sql:
SELECT building, room_number, capacity
FROM classroom_rows
views.description: Canonicalized classroom identifiers and numeric capacity as a simple projection of classroom table (useful for capacity-based filters and joins).

views.name: sections_with_location
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  section.course_id,
  section.sec_id,
  section.semester,
  section.year,
  section.building,
  section.room_number
FROM section
JOIN classroom
  ON section.building = classroom.building
  AND section.room_number = classroom.room_number
views.description: Section rows joined with their classroom location (building and room_number) to relate scheduled sections to classroom attributes like capacity.

views.name: classroom_counts_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  COUNT(classroom.room_number) AS classroom_count
FROM classroom
GROUP BY classroom.building
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of classrooms per building (one row per building) for quick retrieval of counts and joins.

views.name: buildings_with_department_info
views.body_sql:
SELECT c.building AS building,
       d.dept_name AS dept_name,
       d.budget AS budget
FROM classroom_rows c
JOIN department d ON d.building = c.building
views.description: Buildings (as appearing in classrooms) annotated with department(s) located in the same building and department budget — useful for cross-building summaries and filters.
counter_examples: Could you please find out all the buildings that have exactly two different departments occupying them? I need to know specifically the names of those buildings!

views.name: department_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dept_name,
  building,
  budget
FROM department
views.description: One row per department with its name, building and budget normalized for use in filters and joins.
validated_on: Could you please collect information on all the departments whose names start with 'M', have a budget greater than both zero and the average budget of all departments? Make sure the department details include their name and building, and only provide information about the instructor with the highest salary in each department, noting the instructor's ID, name, and salary. Also, categorize the department names as either "Long Name" or "Short Name" based on whether their length is greater than 10 characters.
What are the names and buildings of the first three departments when ordered alphabetically by department name?
What is the total number of distinct courses offered by the Physics department?
Could you provide the average budget for each department?

views.name: department_budget_stats
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.budget AS budget,
  (SELECT AVG(d2.budget) FROM department d2) AS avg_budget_all_departments
FROM department
views.description: Aggregate budget statistics across departments; provides per-department budget along with global average and other aggregates to support comparisons.

views.name: department_with_courses_count
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS building,
  d.budget AS budget,
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  c.title AS title,
  c.credits AS credits
FROM department d
LEFT JOIN course c
  ON d.dept_name = c.dept_name
views.description: Departments joined with their courses; one row per department giving basic department attributes and the (raw) course_id for join-level analyses. Useful for questions that need department-level info alongside courses.

views.name: instructor_by_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT instructor.ID AS ID,
       instructor.name AS name,
       instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
       instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor
views.description: One row per instructor exposing instructor identity, department membership, and salary for joins and top-instructor selection.

views.name: top_instructor_per_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  -- rank of instructor within department by salary (1 = highest)
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY d.dept_name ORDER BY i.salary DESC, i.ID) AS top_instructor_rank,
  i.ID AS top_instructor_id,
  i.name AS top_instructor_name,
  i.salary AS top_instructor_salary
FROM department d
LEFT JOIN instructor i
  ON i.dept_name = d.dept_name
views.description: For each department (dept_name) produce the top instructor by salary. Ties are broken arbitrarily but view exposes rank for deterministic selection in queries.

views.name: building_avg_classroom_capacity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  AVG(classroom.capacity) AS avg_capacity,
  COUNT(classroom.room_number) AS classroom_count
FROM classroom
GROUP BY classroom.building
views.description: Per building aggregated metrics for classrooms: average capacity and classroom count. One row per building.
validated_on: For buildings linked to the Civil Engineering department, what are their names and average classroom capacities, ordered from highest to lowest average capacity?

views.name: department_with_building_and_budget
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.building AS building,
  department.budget AS budget
FROM department
WHERE department.budget IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per department exposing its building and budget (raw), excluding NULL budgets for downstream numeric aggregations.

views.name: rooms_with_department_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  classroom.building AS building,
  classroom.room_number AS room_number,
  classroom.capacity AS capacity,
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.budget AS department_budget
FROM classroom
JOIN department
  ON department.building = classroom.building
views.description: Classrooms augmented with the department(s) that are located in the same building (denormalized relation to support queries joining rooms and departments). One row per classroom and department-building pairing when department.building matches classroom.building.

views.name: sections_in_classrooms
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  c.capacity,
  sec.time_slot_id
FROM sections_with_location s
LEFT JOIN classroom_capacity_projection c
  ON s.building = c.building AND s.room_number = c.room_number
LEFT JOIN section sec
  ON s.course_id = sec.course_id AND s.sec_id = sec.sec_id AND s.semester = sec.semester AND s.year = sec.year
views.description: Section offerings tied to the classroom where they meet, exposing section keys and classroom capacity for scheduling/room-capacity queries. One row per section (identified by course_id, sec_id, semester, year).

views.name: departments_by_building
views.body_sql:
SELECT department.dept_name AS dept_name,
       department.building AS building,
       department.budget AS budget
FROM department
views.description: Department rows joined to their building info (same as department here but named for queries that group or filter by building). Exposes department key plus building and budget for grouping or selection by building.
validated_on: Could you provide the average budget for each department?

views.name: department_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.dept_name AS dept_name,
  department.building AS building,
  department.budget AS budget
FROM department
views.description: Canonical department rows with primary key and core attributes (one row per department). Cleans/canonicalizes columns but does not aggregate.

views.name: departments_by_budget_rank
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.building AS building,
  d.budget AS budget,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY d.budget DESC) AS budget_rank
FROM department d
views.description: Each department with its budget and a rank (dense_rank) by budget descending, so ties share the same rank. One row per department.

views.name: departments_budget_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT department.dept_name AS dept_name,
       department.budget AS budget
FROM department
views.description: Row-level cohort of department budgets exposing dept identifier and budget measure; useful for aggregations (max, avg, sum) or filtering in later queries.

views.name: departments_by_building_18
views.body_sql:
SELECT dept_name, building
FROM department
views.description: Department rows exposing department name and the building associated with the department.

views.name: students_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  student.ID AS ID,
  student.name AS name,
  student.dept_name AS dept_name,
  student.tot_cred AS tot_cred
FROM student
views.description: Canonical student rows with core attributes cleaned/normalized for joins and filtering.

views.name: students_by_department_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  sb.ID AS ID,
  sb.name AS name,
  sb.dept_name AS dept_name
FROM students_basic sb
views.description: Cohort of students annotated with their department for answering department-scoped queries (one row per student).

views.name: students_with_advisors_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT s.ID,
       s.name,
       s.dept_name,
       s.tot_cred,
       a.i_ID
FROM student AS s
LEFT JOIN advisor AS a
  ON s.ID = a.s_ID
views.description: Student rows left-joined to their advisor instructor id (one row per student), useful for queries that need student+advisor relationships or further joins to instructor.

views.name: classroom_capacity_categories
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.building,
  c.room_number,
  c.capacity,
  CASE
    WHEN c.capacity IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN c.capacity <= 20 THEN 'small'
    WHEN c.capacity <= 50 THEN 'medium'
    WHEN c.capacity <= 100 THEN 'large'
    ELSE 'very_large'
  END AS size_category
FROM classroom c
views.description: Classrooms annotated with normalized size_category labels derived from capacity thresholds. Keeps one row per classroom and exposes the computed category for easy aggregation and filtering in downstream queries.

views.name: classroom_counts_by_building_and_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cr.building AS building,
  CASE
    WHEN cr.capacity >= 100 THEN 'Large'
    WHEN cr.capacity >= 50 THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Small'
  END AS size_category,
  COUNT(cr.room_number) AS classroom_count
FROM classroom_rows cr
GROUP BY
  cr.building,
  CASE
    WHEN cr.capacity >= 100 THEN 'Large'
    WHEN cr.capacity >= 50 THEN 'Medium'
    ELSE 'Small'
  END
views.description: Pre-aggregated counts of classrooms per building and per size_category (Large/Medium/Small) using canonical capacity thresholds. Useful for quick lookups of how many classrooms of each size exist in each building.

views.name: advisor_relationships
views.body_sql:
SELECT s_ID, i_ID
FROM advisor
WHERE i_ID IS NOT NULL
views.description: One row per advisor-student assignment from the advisor table; exposes the student ID and the advisor (instructor) ID for downstream filtering and joins.

views.name: instructor_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor
WHERE instructor.salary IS NOT NULL
views.description: Canonicalized instructor rows exposing identifier, name, department, and numeric salary for comparisons and joins.

views.name: advisor_with_instructor_salary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.s_ID AS s_ID,
  a.i_ID AS i_ID,
  i.ID AS ID,
  i.salary AS salary,
  i.name AS name,
  i.dept_name AS dept_name
FROM
  advisor_relationships AS a
JOIN
  instructor_core AS i
ON
  a.i_ID = i.ID
WHERE
  a.i_ID IS NOT NULL
  AND i.salary IS NOT NULL
views.description: Denormalized advisor entries joined to their instructor record so each advisor-student pair includes the advisor's salary and instructor attributes; one row per advisor-student pair.

views.name: students_with_advisors
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  advisor.s_ID AS s_ID,
  student.tot_cred AS student_tot_cred,
  advisor.i_ID AS i_ID
FROM advisor
JOIN student ON student.ID = advisor.s_ID
views.description: One row per student-advisor relationship, linking student rows to their advisor instructor rows. Exposes student identity, student attributes useful for filtering, and advisor (instructor) identity for joining to instructor and teaches.

views.name: instructors_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  instructor.ID AS ID,
  instructor.name AS name,
  instructor.dept_name AS dept_name,
  instructor.salary AS salary
FROM instructor
views.description: Canonical instructor rows with key identifiers and core attributes used for filtering and joins (salary and department).
validated_on: Hey! Can you tell me how many different instructors were teaching courses in the spring semester of 2023? I'm curious to know the total count!

views.name: teaches_sessions
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  teaches.ID,
  teaches.course_id,
  teaches.sec_id,
  teaches.semester,
  teaches.year
FROM teaches
views.description: Row-level teaches records (which instructor taught which section in which semester/year). Useful to identify instructors who taught in a particular semester or year.
validated_on: Hey! Can you tell me how many different instructors were teaching courses in the spring semester of 2023? I'm curious to know the total count!

views.name: course_by_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: Rows of courses exposing course identity, department, and credits so callers can filter departments that offer courses meeting credit criteria.

views.name: department_course_exists
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(c.course_id) AS qualifying_course_count
FROM
  department d
LEFT JOIN
  course c
ON
  c.dept_name = d.dept_name
GROUP BY
  d.dept_name
views.description: For each department, whether it offers at least one course meeting a selectable credit threshold; useful for counting departments that meet course-offering predicates.

views.name: courses_with_credits
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits,
  course.title AS title
FROM course
views.description: One row per course including its department and credit value; useful to filter courses by credit thresholds or join to department-level data.
validated_on: Hey there! Could you tell me which courses don't have any prerequisites? I'm curious to know their titles, thanks!

views.name: departments_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT department.dept_name AS dept_name,
       department.building AS building,
       department.budget AS budget
FROM department
views.description: Canonical department rows (one per department) exposing the primary key and key attributes for joins and existence checks.

views.name: department_course_membership
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  c.dept_name AS course_dept_name,
  c.credits AS credits,
  d.building AS dept_building,
  d.budget AS dept_budget
FROM course c
JOIN department d
  ON c.dept_name = d.dept_name
views.description: Denormalized mapping of courses to their department rows (only departments that exist in department table), one row per course: useful for counting departments that actually offer courses meeting criteria.

views.name: courses_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: Row-level canonical view of courses exposing course identifiers and their department and credits; used as the base cohort for counts, filters, and joins to department-related info.

views.name: course_with_department
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS "course.dept_name",
  course.credits AS credits,
  department.building AS "department.building",
  department.budget AS "department.budget"
FROM course
LEFT JOIN department ON course.dept_name = department.dept_name
views.description: Denormalized view joining courses to their department attributes so queries can filter or aggregate courses by department properties without extra joins.

views.name: course_prerequisite_pairs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course_id,
  prereq_id
FROM
  prereq
views.description: Row-level list of prerequisite relationships linking a course to each of its prerequisite course IDs. One row per (course_id, prereq_id) pair as recorded in prereq.

views.name: course_basic
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name,
  course.credits AS credits
FROM course
views.description: Canonical projection of the course entity exposing its primary key and display attributes (title, department, credits). One row per course.

views.name: prereq_count_per_course
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS distinct_prereq_count
FROM
  course AS c
LEFT JOIN
  prereq AS p
ON
  c.course_id = p.course_id
GROUP BY
  c.course_id
views.description: For each course, the count of distinct prerequisite course IDs. One row per course_id with the distinct prereq count.

views.name: departments_row_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT dept_name, building, budget
FROM department
views.description: One row per department exposing department name and its building and budget for use as a departmental cohort.

views.name: building_department_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  department.building AS building,
  COUNT(DISTINCT department.dept_name) AS distinct_dept_count
FROM department
GROUP BY department.building
views.description: Count of distinct departments per building (one row per building), useful for queries that need how many departments occupy each building.

views.name: course_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  course.course_id AS course_id,
  course.title AS title,
  course.credits AS credits,
  course.dept_name AS dept_name
FROM course
views.description: One row per course with canonical course attributes; cleans explicit NULL/empty department or credits can be applied later.

views.name: prereq_edge
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq
views.description: One row per prerequisite relationship: maps a course to a single prerequisite course_id (distinct edges). Useful for counting distinct prerequisites per course.

views.name: course_prereq_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT prereq.prereq_id) AS prereq_count
FROM prereq
GROUP BY
  prereq.course_id
views.description: Aggregated counts of distinct prerequisites per course. One row per course_id with the number of distinct prereq_id values.

views.name: prereq_count_per_course_45
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.course_id AS course_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.prereq_id) AS prereq_count
FROM
  prereq p
GROUP BY
  p.course_id
views.description: Counts of distinct prerequisites per target course_id. One row per target course with a measure of how many prereqs it has.

views.name: departments_with_instructor_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  d.budget AS budget,
  COUNT(i.ID) AS instructor_count
FROM
  department d
LEFT JOIN
  instructor i
ON
  i.dept_name = d.dept_name
GROUP BY
  d.dept_name,
  d.budget
views.description: Per-department aggregate that counts instructors and exposes raw budget for each department. Keeps one row per department so downstream queries can compute budget-related metrics alongside staffing counts.

views.name: courses_without_prereqs
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id,
  c.title,
  c.dept_name,
  c.credits
FROM course AS c
LEFT JOIN prereq AS p
  ON p.course_id = c.course_id
WHERE p.course_id IS NULL
views.description: All courses that have no prerequisites (i.e., no row in prereq with prereq.course_id = course.course_id).

views.name: sections_with_classroom_and_course
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.course_id,
  s.sec_id,
  s.semester,
  s.year,
  s.building,
  s.room_number,
  s.time_slot_id,
  c.capacity AS classroom_capacity,
  co.dept_name AS course_dept_name
FROM section AS s
JOIN course AS co
  ON s.course_id = co.course_id
LEFT JOIN classroom AS c
  ON s.building = c.building
  AND s.room_number = c.room_number
views.description: Sections joined to their course and the classroom where they meet (denormalized section + course + classroom info).
validated_on: Hey! Can you tell me how many different instructors were teaching courses in the spring semester of 2023? I'm curious to know the total count!

views.name: department_section_classroom_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  s.course_id AS course_id,
  s.sec_id AS sec_id,
  s.semester AS semester,
  s.year AS year,
  s.building AS building,
  s.room_number AS room_number,
  c.capacity AS capacity
FROM sections_with_location s
JOIN course ON s.course_id = course.course_id
JOIN department d ON course.dept_name = d.dept_name
LEFT JOIN classroom c ON s.building = c.building AND s.room_number = c.room_number
views.description: Cohort of section -> classroom occurrences attributed to the course's department. Each row represents one usage of a classroom by a section of a course, exposing department and classroom capacity for aggregation.

views.name: department_course_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.dept_name AS dept_name,
  COUNT(c.course_id) AS dept_course_count
FROM
  department d
LEFT JOIN
  course c
ON
  c.dept_name = d.dept_name
GROUP BY
  d.dept_name
views.description: Number of courses offered by each department (grouped at department level).

views.name: prereq_relations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  prereq.course_id AS course_id,
  prereq.prereq_id AS prereq_id
FROM prereq
views.description: Row-level prerequisite relationships: each row links a course to one of its prerequisite courses.

views.name: course_with_prereq_flag
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.course_id AS course_id,
  c.title AS title,
  CASE WHEN p.course_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS has_prereq
FROM course AS c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT course_id
  FROM prereq
) AS p
ON c.course_id = p.course_id
views.description: Left-joined view that marks whether a course has at least one prerequisite (boolean flag) while keeping one row per course.
